say: Most problems have a simple cause. Wrong or old measurements. Cotton not pre-washed. Wrong tension or a blunt needle. Too many orders accepted.
So measure in a fixed order and date it. Offer to pre-wash cotton such as some Ankara. Test stitch on an offcut and press each seam.
And never skip the fitting. Before finishing, a seam is easy to adjust. After overlocking and pressing, the same change takes longer and can leave marks.
Turn the garment inside out and look at every seam. Try every zip and hook. Measure the bust, waist and length against the order page, then press and photograph it.
If an apprentice sewed it, the owner or senior tailor does this check, not the person who sewed it.

panel.heading: Before any garment leaves
items: Measurements match order page
Seams finished and pressed
Hem level, threads trimmed
Zip and fastenings work smoothly
No marks, stains or chalk
Photo taken for records

say: For example, Ronke in Lagos had late outfits last December, and two clients left. With one trained helper, she can finish about 7 gowns a week.

panel.heading: Ronke's December rush plan
items: Count capacity: about 21 gowns in three weeks
Announce in October when bookings close
Confirm each slot only with a deposit
Fittings at least four days before due
Keep one slot free for emergencies

say: In October she announces that December bookings close when 21 slots are filled, or on 30 November, whichever comes first.

say: Many disputes start with word-of-mouth terms. Write a one-page agreement, read it aloud with the apprentice and a parent or guardian, and give each side a copy.

cards.d: A one-page agreement: duration, fees, hours, pay, tools, rules and completion.
Offcuts first, never client fabric. Sign off each skill with a date.
No beating or insults. Supervise the iron and machines. Never keep a child from school.

say: Start her on offcuts and keep a skills record with dates. It shows her progress and protects you.

say: Beating, insults and threats are abuse and have no place in a workshop. Teach safety on day one. New learners use the iron and machines only under supervision.
If a socket sparks, switch off at the main and do not touch the appliance.

say: You can pay a trained helper a fixed wage, or per piece. Per-piece pay suits busy seasons, but you must check quality closely.
Grace's gown price already has 8,000 naira of labour, for 8 hours. Uche sews the main construction in about 5 hours, so Grace pays 5,000 naira per gown sewn to standard.
Uche sews 10 gowns and earns 50,000 naira. One needs rework, which Uche fixes before payment. Grace's own share stays in the price, so her margin is protected.
Track five numbers monthly: sales, profit, on-time delivery rate, repeat client rate, and average order value.
For example, Aisha in Kano delivered 14 of 20 orders on time in April. That is 70%.

In May she capped weekly bookings and added fittings four days before due dates. On-time delivery rose to about 94%, repeat clients rose, and profit grew by about 30,000 naira, even with fewer orders.
Write a one-page report. A headline, your five numbers side by side, and what went well, with evidence such as a client review.

panel.heading: Your monthly report
items: Headline: one sentence on the month
The five numbers, this month and last
What went well, with evidence
What went wrong, honestly
One action for next month

say: Be honest about what went wrong. Then choose one action only. If you change everything at once, you cannot tell what worked.

say: To remember. Check every garment before it leaves. Book within your capacity. Treat apprentices fairly and keep them safe. And let your numbers, not your busy feeling, guide your next step.
